strauh.al — an atlas, not a feed

A knowledge system built the opposite way from the old web. Instead of a flat pile of pages linking to index pages, this is a **layered atlas**: a spine of *ideas* at the center, and everything else — people, works, reading, images — arranged as what *feeds* those ideas. From here, any of ~10261 notes is three hops away.

→ **The Idea Atlas** — the ideas the whole system hangs from, grouped into four themes. This is the front door; read the vault *through* the ideas.

strauh.al — an atlas, not a feed

A knowledge system built the opposite way from the old web. Instead of a flat pile of pages linking to index pages, this is a **layered atlas**: a spine of *ideas* at the center, and everything else — people, works, reading, images — arranged as what *feeds* those ideas. From here, any of ~10261 notes is three hops away.

① The spine — start here

→ **The Idea Atlas** — the ideas the whole system hangs from, grouped into four themes. This is the front door; read the vault *through* the ideas.

② The domains — what feeds the ideas

meta:
AI Slop

**Ernest's running critique of AI-generated culture — and his uneasy implication in it as an artist who uses neural networks.**

Summary He uses "slop" for both AI imagery and the attention feed. The "all eyes on rafah" AI meme (2024-10-20) is his emblem of a race to the bottom: "now people are just arguing over ai generated activism slop. we're at the bottom. we've finally arrived." It has cost him the ability to look: "now when i see a work of art… i zoom in, look for neural artifacts, go on their social media and investigate if they're actually a human artist. i can feel myself going crazy" (2025-01-29). Yet he uses StyleGAN and pix2pix himself — his position is that "**ai as one step in the process, not the whole process itself**" (ideas-sketchbook), and that "to create art requires love. and pain. something that these dork ass losers making ai art have probably never felt." …

Amor Fati

**"Love of fate" — the Nietzschean stance Ernest copies into the diary as an aspiration: to see what is necessary as beautiful, and to become a "Yes-sayer."**

Summary On 2024-09-04 he transcribes Nietzsche's New Year passage in full: *"i want to learn more and more how to see what is necessary in things as what is beautiful in them — thus i will be one of those who make things beautiful. Amor fati: let that be my love from now on… some day i want only to be a Yes-sayer!"* It sits in tension with the diary's anger and despair, and reads in hindsight as a thesis the whole diary is testing — resolved in the final entry (2025-08-13) when "my will to live has been reignited" and he reframes the despair as what gave the year its meaning.

Key points
• The aesthetic of *making things beautiful* connects to "beauty fills the god shaped hole made by science" and "the raw material of r …

Art Fills the God-Shaped Hole

**Beauty as secular re-enchantment — art doing the work religion used to do after science emptied the room.**

Summary Stated flat in the sketchbook: "beauty fills the god shaped hole made by science," alongside "the raw material of reality must be made beautiful by the artist" and "superstition is a respect for the unknown." It is the current that runs from the otherwise-isolated esoterica shelf (alchemy, Crowley, the occult) through the sense of the internet as a sacred presence and toward The Ceremony. The enemy of this idea is AI Slop — beauty mass-produced until it re-empties the room.

Key points
• Disenchantment is the premise; the artist's job is to re-enchant the raw material.
• Superstition reframed not as error but as "respect for the unknown."
• The bridge between the spirituality reading, the ceremony, and the sacralized net.

Atomization

**The social ground the rest of the critique stands on: a world broken into separated individuals — "atomized male / atomized female," in the sketchbook's phrase.**

Summary It is the condition the political and literary reading keeps circling — Houellebecq's atomised individuals, Mark Fisher's capitalist realism, the dating-app loneliness — and the precondition that makes The Attention Economy profitable and AI Slop frictionless: a population of isolated users is easier to feed and to sell to. It is also what The Internet as Confidant tries to answer — confiding in the network because the neighbors are gone.

Key points
• Isolation as infrastructure: the feed presupposes the atom.
• The bridge from the politics/literature shelves to the attention critique.
• Why the internet becomes a confidant — it fills a hole left by atomization.

Autofiction

**Ernest's own term for what the diary became: "this diary began as an earnest (heh) attempt at recording daily events, but has morphed into autofiction. i am actively narrativizing in my life. don't believe half the things you read in this diary."**

Summary By 2024-11-28 he no longer trusts the diary as record. He notes that everyone on social media "spoonfeeds you a narrativized version of their life," but typing it out and reading it back makes the narrativization conscious and "a bit more mental." He prunes entries that "did not sound like they were written by a mentally well individual" (2024-12-28), and admits the diary's direction is shaped by the knowledge that others might read it (see The Internet as Confidant).

Key points
• Sincerity is unstable: an angry early entry gets annotated — "i can't remember if this was meant to be sincere, ironic, or post-ironic" (lin …

Dead Architecture

Ben Read reports Ernest describing generated video as “dead architecture with the illusion of movement.” The phrase names a paradox: a model produces apparent motion from predetermined transitions and interpolated data, creating duration without a newly performed event.

The generated body seems to move, but the motion is a pixel structure assembled from traces of prior movement. This makes time inside the work feel simultaneously fluid and already completed.

Interpolating the Instruction Set

**A seed from the sketchbook that sharpens Latent Space: "you're not actually interpolating through images, you're interpolating through the instruction set to MAKE those images."**

Summary The correction matters. Naively, a latent walk looks like a dissolve between pictures. The sketchbook insists it is one level deeper: you are moving through the space of *recipes* — the generative instructions — and the images are only what those recipes render. It reframes Implicit Distance (a walk through the StyleGAN of a life) and the GAN Color Studies as movements through procedure, not imagery, and it is the precise hinge where Latent Space meets the Human-Machine Tug of War: the artist steers the instruction set; the model executes it.

meta:
Latent Space

**Ernest's central technical-poetic metaphor: identity, art, and feeling as positions and trajectories inside a continuous interpolated space.**

Summary In the diary's most explicit statement (2024-09-17) he imagines a future where every human trait — "politics, sports, language, employment, art, music, sexuality, religion, nationality, and race" — is "labeled as vector coordinates in some sort of latent space," and people can watch their own trajectories through it: "we'll no longer have to worry about ever misunderstanding each other ever again." The same idea drives his art: Implicit Distance is literally a walk through the latent space of a StyleGAN trained on his life, and warping audio "interpolates between each audio sample."

Key points
• Interpolation as both technique and worldview — distance is something you move *through*.
• His kits.ai Voice is the self reduce …

Memory and Preservation

**The drive to capture and keep — memories, images, even rooms and voices — that underwrites the whole archive.**

Summary The strauh.al Archive is itself an act of preservation ("the closest thing to my consciousness that i can capture in html"). In the diary the impulse turns literal: he "milks" a café memory of his father (2024-09-24), and on 2024-12-25 tries "to do a neural radiance field of my grandmas house so that I can hold onto this memory forever." It shades into dread, too — the inherited compulsions of his stock-obsessed grandfather (2024-12-29), behaviors "repeating… but with faster tools."

Key points
• Technology as memory prosthesis: NeRF, the archive, the diary, the kits.ai Voice.
• The Proustian detail (see Marcel Proust) as the seed of recollection.
• In tension with Autofiction — what's preserved is already narrativized.

• strauh. …

Post-Irony

**The unstable register Ernest writes and lives in — where sincere, ironic, and post-ironic can no longer be told apart, even by him.**

Summary Annotating an angry early entry months later (2024-09-01 → 09-07): "i think i was trying to be really angsty when i wrote this. i can't remember if this was meant to be sincere, ironic, or post-ironic." He crowns "rebecca black… the queen of post irony" (2024-10-27) and signs off a recurring credo: "**if you're not being cringe, you're not being based**" (2025-01-30). The mode is both a defense (covering hurt "with memes and ironic language") and the thing he keeps trying to write his way out of.

Connections
• Autofiction — narrativizing the self in a tone you can't pin down.
• The Attention Economy — irony as the native dialect of the feed.

Reading Like a Computer

**The attention damage of the feed, felt at the level of reading itself: scanning for the point instead of inhabiting the text.**

Summary In the Camus thread, Ernest admits he has "lost the ability to read fiction" and "anxiously wait[s] for camus to 'arrive at the point.'" He generalizes it (2024-12-29): "we just scan texts like computers instead of engaging with them as humans." It is The Attention Economy turned inward — the specific cognitive cost behind the library he owns but can't always read, and the human side of the same machine logic he critiques as AI Slop.

Key points
• Comprehension degraded into extraction — reading as ctrl-F.
• The library as evidence: hundreds of ebooks, a shrinking capacity to sit with one.
• Why the slow, human act of reading becomes a deliberate counter-practice.

**Collapse treated as the precondition for the next build — not despair, but raw material. From the sketchbook: "part of the fun when my life falls apart is that it gets even better when i rebuild it."**

It is the *active* cousin of Amor Fati: where amor fati is loving what is necessary, this is the will to reconstruct from it. Synesthesia

**The recurring dream of mapping one sense onto another — color as sound, sound as color, feeling as coordinate.**

Summary The oldest thread in Ernest's influences, made new by the machine. Alexander Scriabin assigned colors to musical keys; Wassily Kandinsky said he *heard* color as music. The sketchbook keeps reaching for it — "color as a temporal axis," "psychological notation" — and the work enacts it: the GAN Color Studies turn line into color, Implicit Distance warps image and audio along the same path. It is Latent Space experienced through the senses rather than the math, and the perceptual side of Transmitting My Neural Signals by Hand.

Key points
• A single underlying axis the senses are different projections of.

meta:
The Archive as Consciousness

**The archive isn't a record of the mind — it's the mind offloaded. Ernest's own line: the site is "the closest thing to my consciousness that i can capture in html."**

Summary This reframes the whole project. If the strauh.al Archive is consciousness externalized, then collecting is thinking, the link is a synapse, and this very vault is a second-order archive — an archive *of* the archive, a map of a mind that was already a map. It is the structural premise beneath Memory and Preservation (the drive) and Autofiction (the narration), and it's why The Internet as Confidant feels less like an audience than a shared nervous system.

• Collection as cognition; the corpus as an outboard brain.

meta:
The Attention Economy

**The endless, personalized feed — Ernest's recurring antagonist, blamed for hollowing out art, activism, and his own focus.**

Summary He wants TikTok, Reels, and Shorts banned outright: "millions (perhaps billions) of man-hours will be taken back" (2024-09-13) — and admits the feed is why he abandoned The Record Label: "how can artists/musicians compete with an endless stream of entertainment that is tailored to the user?" His Andy Warhol update names it as the last shared American experience: "everyone (rich and poor) doomscrolls on the same apps on the same phones." Social-media activism becomes "a race to the bottom" (see AI Slop), and even his own focus is collateral: "any frustration in my mind can be numbed with an endless feed."

• Andy Warhol — the doomscroll as universal Coke.

The Flâneur as Web Surfer

**The 19th-century stroller of the arcades, rebooted as the aimless drifter of the feed — the figure at the heart of the Arcades Project (Revisited).**

Summary Benjamin built his arcades around the *flâneur*, the idle, hyper-observant walker who reads the crowd and the shop windows. The Arcades Project rewrites that figure directly: the websites are "vast virtual corridors," and the user is the flâneur who wanders them "during times of boredom or curiosity." It is the human posture The Attention Economy is designed to capture and the net is designed to receive — and a cousin to the rail-rider of Trainpilled, another kind of drift through a built landscape.

The Panel as Canvas

**Manga, anime, and the graphic novel read with the same seriousness as painting — not a guilty pleasure bracketed off from "real" art.**

Summary The reading list puts sequential art on equal footing with Hegel and Proust: Katsuhiro Otomo's *Akira*, Junji Ito's *Tomie*, Tatsuki Fujimoto's *Look Back*, and Osamu Dazai's prose sit a few lines from Frank Miller's *Batman: Year One* and *Sin City*. The Spatial Web

**Knowledge as a place you move through — the wish to navigate information in three dimensions instead of scrolling a list.**

Summary The sketchbook keeps circling it: "spatial z index for the spatial web," "3d atlas," "hegel3datlas," and "for the 3d atlas, have an option that rearranges the words based on significance." meta:
The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal

**A seed from the sketchbook: the friction and slowness of making is not an obstacle to the work — it *is* the work.**

Summary Written plainly in the sketchbook: "the tedium of the art is the goal," set right beside "ai as one step in the process, not the whole process itself." The same vein runs through "the best art happens when the medium guides the artist" and "it's better to hit a wrong note than to play something that's lifeless." The labor is not overhead to be optimized away; it is where the meaning is deposited. This is the exact value that AI Slop inverts — slop is all output and no process — and the value that Video Portraiture enacts literally, by tracing video frames onto vellum by hand.

• Process over product: the time spent is the medium, not friction in it.

**Landscape read as atmosphere and mood rather than geography — the sketchbook's own "vellum chinese ink painting landscape," extended through the named influence Kawase Hasui and the Muromachi ink painter Josetsu.**

meta:
To Render Myself Unnecessary

**Teaching as the inverse of authorship: the goal is your own disappearance. From the sketchbook — "to truly educate is to render myself unnecessary."**

Summary A value that turns out to be inherited. Ernest's father taught high-school math; his mother taught a Chinese–English first-grade immersion program. Ernest now teaches visual art to children on digital whiteboards and, by 2026, piano to mentally and physically handicapped children and adults. Where the Human-Machine Tug of War is about *holding* authorship, this is about *giving it away* — and it rhymes with The Tedium of the Art Is the Goal: the worth is in the patient process, not the credit.

Ernest Strauhal

**Ernest Charles Strauhal · 許志仁 — born 8:30am, October 15, 2000, Children's Hospital, San Francisco. The person the whole vault is a map of.** The youngest and oldest child of four: three miscarriages came before him, so he arrived as both the first to survive and the last they had.

The shape of it Chinese-American, raised on the move: the family left San Francisco for Sacramento in 2003. School ran from Elliot Ranch Elementary through West Campus High; piano started in 2008. He entered the design program at CCA (formerly CCAC) in 2018 and left it in 2019 — the first of the abandonments. Graduate school at SAIC followed in 2022, then a year of shows and releases in New York and Chicago in 2023, then the 2024 collapse — no work, his aunt and uncle's basement in suburban Illinois, antidepressants, and the start of the diary. 2025 was the bottom and the turn: failure in Ch …

Failures and Abandoned Projects

> "part of the fun when my life falls apart is that it gets even better when i rebuild it." — sketchbook

**A deliberate ledger of the things that stopped — what they were, why they ended, and what they produced anyway. Patterns in failure are more instructive than patterns in success.**

The record label An attempt to start a label; it got as far as a webpage and a Bandcamp page before he quit (diary, 2024-09-13). The stated reason became a whole idea: "how can artists compete with an endless stream of entertainment tailored to the user?" → see The Record Label and The Attention Economy. **Produced anyway:** the clearest articulation of why the feed defeats sustained work.

The slop period (2022 – early 2023) By his own account "my slop period… truly artistically bankrupt" — stretching 15-second snippets of obscure songs into six-minute pieces. It ended …

Family

**The lineage behind Ernest — two sides that meet in San Francisco, and that quietly seed half the vault's recurring themes.**

Mother's side — Guangzhou to Chinatown
• **Mother:** born in Guangzhou, China; moved to San Francisco's Chinatown at 11. She taught a Chinese–English first-grade immersion program — one root of the teaching lineage, and of Latent Space read as autobiography (language and nationality as coordinates of the self).
• **Maternal grandfather:** a day trader who listened to the radio each morning and carried his abacus to the Hong Kong stock exchange to buy and sell shares — a life lived by the morning information stream, a strange ancestor to The Attention Economy.
• **Maternal great-(great-)grandfather:** the details are murky, but he helped build the railroads in California and gained citizenship after the **1906 San Francisco great fire**. He is the literal …

The Ceremony

**The threshold the seven dreams were recorded *before* — an ayahuasca ceremony undertaken to restructure how everything is seen. This node exists so that whatever follows gets wired into the vault, not processed privately and lost.**

Map - Maintenance

The 30-day habit (most important)

A second brain that isn't updated becomes an archive of who you *were* — and there is already one of those. This one should track who you're *becoming*. So the simplest, load-bearing habit: **re-open the vault about every 30 days and add what changed.**

meta:
No More Human Art

Ben Read's essay examines Ernest's use of Pix2Pix and StyleGAN as a way of testing authorship, control, and generated time rather than merely automating image production.

Argument

Read places Ernest's practice against public anxiety about artificial intelligence in art. The essay argues that the work matters because it stages a visible negotiation between hand, dataset, algorithm, and editorial judgment.

The central sequence is:

1. Ernest produces a drawing, movement, voice recording, or personal dataset. 2. A GAN introduces outputs that can be directed but not fully predicted. 3. Ernest edits, accepts, rejects, sequences, or reframes those outputs.

Read calls this relation a Human-Machine Tug of War. The machine is collaborator and exterior force, but the finished work remains subject to Ernest's aesthetic judgment.

Arcades Project (Revisited)

**Ernest's web work modeled on Walter Benjamin's Arcades Project: a montage of quotes, screenshots, and fragments filed into lettered "convolutes," but with the 19th-century Paris arcade swapped for the internet.**

Summary The page opens by re-writing Benjamin's famous description of the arcades as a description of *websites* — "vast virtual corridors extending through the landscape of the internet… a world in miniature, in which users will find everything they need." It keeps Benjamin's method intact: lettered convolutes (a = the digital arcades and "web surfers," b = fashion, d = boredom and eternal return), each a collage of found text — tweets, greentext, AI-slop captions — indexed in his hand like [A1,1]. It is the vault's clearest piece of *criticism-as-art*: a structure borrowed wholesale from a dead theorist and turned on the present.

Why it matters …

Dreams Series

**A series of ~43 drawings made on the threshold of sleep, where dream and waking reality overwrite each other on the page.**

Summary For this series Ernest lay on his side holding a pen above a notebook, drifting in and out of sleep. As he dozed, "the dream would overwrite itself over reality" — he would accidentally draw over preexisting sketches and notes while half asleep, so each sheet records the collision of the two states.

Key points
• Method *is* the meaning: no separation between intention and mark — a pure case of Spontaneity and Elegance ("the smallest time lag between the ache to draw and its expression").
• Hosted as image scans (dream_00000–dream_00042) in the strauh.al archive.
• Resonates with the diary's preoccupation with dreams, VR dreams, and altered states.

A drawing-to-model-to-editing process described by Ben Read: Ernest builds geometric line drawings by following an initial contour with successive semi-parallel lines, sends the drawing through Pix2Pix for colorization, then adjusts the output through color correction and editorial judgment.

**A 2023 audiovisual composition (EP) built from warped synthesizer sketches and a StyleGAN trained on images from Ernest's own life.**
